newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel clears sale of Israel Edible to CPC.
newsitem.headline: Israel clears sale of Israel Edible to CPC.

text.p: Israel's anti-trust authority has approved the sale of Koor Industries's 24.5 percent holding in Israel Edible Products to America's CPC International, Koor said on Wednesday.

Koor said CPC paid 122.22 million shekels ($37.5 million) for the holding in Israel Edible, which is also known as Tami. Koor, Israel's largest holding company, said it would post capital gains of some 45 million shekels in the first quarter of 1997 from the sale.
The acquisition brings CPC's total stake in Israel Edible to about 84 percent.

CPC acquired a 51 percent holding in Israel Edible in 1993 for $43 million and then helped introduce CPC products, like Hellman's mayonnaise, to the line. CPC brands now make up 12-15 percent of Israel Edible's product line, the company said.

Israel Edible produced 90 percent of Israel's margarine as well as soups, sauces, breakfast cereals, snacks and chocolates. The company said sales last year were $250 million, making it Israel's third-largest dry goods producer.
Koor has said the sale is part of its strategy to pull out of activities outside of its core businesses in telecommunications, electronics, agrochemicals, building materials and energy distribution.
Sources said this week that Koor was in talks to sell its Shemen Industries subsidiary, which makes edible oils and personal care products.
Tami has said the CPC acquisition will not lead to any fundamental change in the company's strategy.
